question: The Asian Development Bank was founded in ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1966**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** was established on **19 December 1966**, with the objective of fostering economic growth and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region. 
• The founding members of ADB include **31 countries**, with the headquarters located in **Mandaluyong, Philippines**. 
• ADB focuses on **poverty reduction, sustainable development, and regional integration** through financial support, technical assistance, and policy consultation. 
• Its initial capital was **USD 1 billion**, and it has since grown significantly, with **more than 68 members** as of now, including both regional and non-regional members. 
• Japan and the United States are the **largest contributors** to ADB’s resources and play a crucial role in its governance and operations. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Functions of ADB:** 
• ADB provides **loans, grants, and equity investments** to its member countries for development projects in sectors like **infrastructure, education, health, and agriculture**. 
• It also offers **technical assistance** to help member nations design, implement, and improve development projects. 
• ADB promotes **regional cooperation** by supporting cross-border projects and encouraging trade and investment partnerships among member nations. 
• **Key Milestones:** 
• ADB’s first President was **Takeo Fukuda** from Japan. 
• It initiated its first loan project in **1968**, providing funds for agriculture development in Thailand. 
• Over the years, ADB has evolved to address challenges such as **climate change, disaster management, and urbanization**. 
• **Membership Details:** 
• ADB currently has **68 members**, with **49 regional members** and **19 non-regional members**. 
• Prominent members include **India, China, Japan, Australia, and the United States**. 
• **Funding Mechanism:** 
• ADB raises funds through **capital contributions** from member countries and by issuing bonds in international financial markets. 
• It also mobilizes resources from other financial institutions for co-financing development projects. 
• **Important Reports:** 
• ADB publishes the **Asian Development Outlook**, an annual report analyzing economic trends and prospects for its member countries. 
• The **Key Indicators for Asia and the Pacific** report provides statistical data to support regional development efforts. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Japan’s Role:** Japan has been a significant contributor to ADB, reflecting its commitment to regional development. It holds the largest share of ADB capital along with the United States. 
• **Focus on Sustainability:** ADB emphasizes sustainable development through environmental conservation, renewable energy projects, and climate resilience initiatives. 
• **Recent Initiatives:** ADB launched a **COVID-19 Active Response and Expenditure Support (CARES) Program** to help member countries combat the pandemic. 
• **Headquarters:** The decision to set up ADB’s headquarters in the Philippines was influenced by its central location in the Asia-Pacific region.
